title: The Orphic egg wound round by a serpent (engraving for Bryant's A New System, or an Analysis of Ancient Mythology)
why: One serpent winds a tilted spiral of bands around a hatched egg on blank white, the game's win state (snakes covering the egg) as a single flat emblem that could be cut down to a logo mark.

title: Brera Altarpiece (Montefeltro Altarpiece), detail of the hanging ostrich egg (crop, 2x upscale)
why: A small pale egg dangles on a thin gold thread inside a grey scallop-shell niche, one tiny white oval as the whole point of a calm architectural space, close to the cover's egg held in a cave hollow.

title: Ouroboros from the alchemical text of Zosimos (Paris, BnF Parisinus graecus 2327)
artist: Anonymous Byzantine copyist, after Zosimos of Panopolis
year: late 15th c. copy of a 3rd c. text
why: A thick black serpent ring swallowing its tail with a blank white interior, a ready circular frame (a roundel) for logo or capsule work; low-res, text-heavy page, so use the ring only.

title: Aurora consurgens (Zurich, Zentralbibliothek Ms. Rh. 172), fol. 21v: dragon in a fired vessel with a bird alighting on it
why: A blue dragon coils inside a round-bellied pot over red flames while a man tips powder in, flat medieval colour blocks on green: vessel, serpent and fire in one readable emblem.

title: The Garden of Earthly Delights, central panel, detail of the cracked egg
why: A huge pale cracked-shell egg fills the frame with small figures spilling out of the break, a rare painted treatment of an egg as a rebirth vessel with crackle texture.

title: Atalanta Fugiens, Emblem VIII: 'Take the egg and pierce it with a fiery sword'
why: A single white egg sits alone on a plinth in a deep perspective hall while a sworded man and fire flank it, the egg as the only light object at the centre of a dark monochrome engraving.

title: Asiatic devices allusive to the cosmogony: mundane eggs, one entwined by the Ophion serpent (etching)
license: Public domain (Wellcome Collection Public Domain Mark)
why: Right panel is a serpent spiralling round an egg as an isolated icon and left panel an egg on a stepped plinth with a crescent, two ready egg-emblem silhouettes on one sheet.

title: A crowned alchemical flask containing a young king in red (watercolour after Splendor Solis)
why: A figure stands inside a long teardrop glass vessel surrounded by a gold aureole with a crown above, a soul-vessel (phylactery) as one tall glowing glass shape on a pale ground.

title: Relief of Phanes/Aion inside the zodiac ring (Modena, Galleria Estense)
why: A winged youth is wrapped by a serpent whose head reaches his chest, standing inside an egg-shaped oval ringed by a zodiac band: the Orphic egg and the coil as a symmetric framed emblem with a built-in border.

title: Laocoon and his Sons (Vatican, Roman copy)
artist: Hagesandros, Athenodoros, Polydoros of Rhodes (Hellenistic original)
why: Thick pale serpent coils cross three bone-coloured bodies against a dark ground, a lesson in how heavy coils read as big graphic S-curves over a pale subject.

title: The golden cosmic egg (Hiranyagarbha), Bhagavata Purana series
why: A single flat gold ellipse sits on a blue-grey field of white concentric contour lines, the egg as a pure glowing shape with no detail at all, the simplest possible egg icon.

title: Votive hand of Sabazius (Walters Art Museum 54.2453)
why: The real Sabazios hand: two raised fingers, a snake curling up the wrist and tiny figures on the palm above a temple niche, green patina on bone-pale ground, a direct model for the bronze hand prop.

title: Head tefillin (phylactery) resting on a rock
why: The literal phylactery: a black cube with knotted black leather straps on pale stone, useful for the box-and-strap silhouette, not as a style reference.

title: Arm Reliquary (South Netherlandish)
why: A gilded hand with two raised fingers rises from a narrow silver sleeve against grey seamless, one gold shape on a vertical silhouette, near the blessing-hand gesture.

title: Reliquary head of Saint Yrieix (silver with gilt band and gems)
why: A silver face with empty carved eyes on a jewelled collar, a hollow vessel that holds a skull, so the lich-as-reliquary idea in cool silver with one warm gold band.

title: Triptych: Annunciation with the Prophets David and Isaiah (painted enamel, Walters 44316)
why: Both side prophets hold long curling scrolls lettered in gothic capitals, the original speech-banderole sense of phylactery, with the ribbon looping round each figure like a title banner.

title: Rock crystal amuletic sphere pendant, gold-banded
why: A clear crystal ball strapped in beaded gold with a hanging loop: an amulet and a glass orb in one object, pale glass and gold on a soft gradient, a model for the orb icon.

title: Monstrance
why: A gold sunburst ring of rays around a small clear window on a slender stem, a radial halo around a see-through centre that could frame the egg on a capsule.

title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
why: One diagonal shaft of amber light enters a dark room from a high window and lands on the chosen figure, a single beam driving the whole composition, like the hole far above the cave.

title: The Philosopher in Meditation
why: A tiny seated figure in a huge dark vault with one golden window and a spiral stair catching the glow, the scale of small body to black cave in exactly the target amber and near-black.

title: The Alchemist, in Search of the Philosopher's Stone, Discovers Phosphorus
why: A kneeling alchemist is lit from below by a glowing glass flask in a dim gothic vault, the glass vessel as the light source of the whole picture.

title: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
why: A ring of faces is lit by one candle behind a glass globe that holds a white bird, a glass orb as the lit sacrifice at the centre of a dark room.

title: The Magdalen with the Smoking Flame
why: One candle flame and a skull in her lap in warm orange on near-black, the restrained two-tone palette where bone-cream sits under amber light.

title: Antrum Platonicum (Plato's Cave)
artist: Jan Saenredam, after Cornelis van Haarlem
why: An engraved cave with a lantern hanging in the middle and a bright arched opening at upper left, plus a Latin lettering band along the top and bottom that is ready-made border typography.

title: The Empyrean (Paradiso, canto 31)
why: Two tiny figures stand under a vast radial engraving converging on a pinpoint of light, a concentric composition around one bright centre where the egg could sit.

title: An Allegory of the Vanities of Human Life
why: A slanting pale shaft of light crosses a dark wall toward a table where a skull, books, a lamp and a jar lie in a heap: the single closest match, a diagonal beam plus laid-out objects plus a skull.

title: A Beam Through the Darkness, Son Doong Cave
why: A bright blue-white shaft drops through a hole in the ceiling onto a rock shelf with one tiny standing figure, the real-world version of the shaft from a hole far above, with soft volumetric fog.

title: The Burning Glass
why: A girl holds a small glass to focus a thin sunbeam onto a heap of twigs, a lens focusing a ray as a tiny charming action, with the thin diagonal beam as the compositional line.

title: Stephoidea (radiolarians), Kunstformen der Natur
why: White linework glass skeletons with small pink and yellow accents float on pure black, ornament that reads as prismatic gems in darkness, a good reference for gem and orb glyphs on a black field.

title: The Crystal Ball
why: A woman holds a glass sphere at chest height beside a skull and an open book, the orb a small bright circle against deep red velvet, glass and skull in one quiet interior.

title: Stained-glass window light on the floor, Eglise des Jacobins, Toulouse
why: Coloured light pools in amber, red and white over a dark tiled floor, showing how prismatic light sits on a black ground, close to the amber plus prismatic accents palette.

title: Magnetite lodestone lifting paperclips
why: A raw lodestone with a rough warm surface lifts paperclips into the air against pure black, the rock prop plus its power in one low-key photograph.

title: Frontispiece of Ars Magna Lucis et Umbrae
why: Straight rays cross a dense engraved frontispiece from a radiant source via mirrors, with a cave opening and beam at lower right, light as geometry in a very ornate frame.

title: Still Life with Quince, Cabbage, Melon and Cucumber
why: Four plain objects hang and sit in a stone niche with a vast empty black space beside them, extreme negative space and objects treated as icons, like the six prop objects.

title: Agnus Dei (The Lamb of God)
why: A bound white lamb lies lit from the left against near-black, a pale offering as one calm shape, bone-cream on black.

title: Melencolia I
why: A brooding winged figure sits among tools, a polyhedron and a sphere laid down around her with a comet and rainbow arc behind, the laid-down objects of a figure who has stopped working.

title: The Emperor, from The Dance of Death
why: Death looms over a throne while the emperor's orb and an hourglass lie on the floor, giving up power as skeleton plus dropped regalia in clear black and white woodcut shapes.

title: Still Life with Lemons, Oranges and a Rose
why: A cup, a basket and a plate of fruit sit in a row on a dark ledge in warm light against black, the laid-out-in-a-line offering arrangement the six objects could use on the cave floor.

title: Three Roman votive offerings representing faces (terracotta)
why: Three terracotta votive heads in soft clean light on white, votive faces left as gifts, a shape reference for the mask offering.

title: Jajo weza (The Serpent's Egg), Polish film poster
why: A white tilted panel of heavy black lettering sits over flat thick-outlined brown figures, with the O of JAJO holding a tiny orange glyph: title lettering as the centre of the design.

title: Alien, one-sheet
why: One cracked egg lit by a thin green-yellow seam floats in total black over a ridged floor with widely spaced title letters: the one-object-in-darkness capsule to learn from, almost the cave-egg premise.

title: Close Encounters of the Third Kind, one-sheet
why: A road runs to a glowing horizon under a star field with centred, calm title text, one light source at the vanishing point and a stack of centred type.

title: Vertigo, poster
why: A white spiral of fine line coils round a falling black figure on an orange disc, a coil that wraps its subject, the egg-covered-by-snakes idea in flat graphic form.

title: Seconds, alternate poster
why: A black box with its lid ajar holds one small figure above a bold red title on white, a container with a small figure inside in four flat shapes plus one red accent.
